summary: Chess is the archetypal perfect-information abstract strategy game: two players maneuver 16 asymmetric pieces on an 8x8 board trying to checkmate the opponent's king. Games can range from quick tactical skirmishes to deep, patient positional battles depending on skill level.
praised: Nearly infinite strategic depth from simple rules
Massive body of theory, literature, and community
criticised: Steep skill ceiling makes mismatches lopsided and unfun for the weaker player
Can be slow and cerebral for casual players
Opening theory memorization can feel like a barrier to entry

interaction.detail: Every piece moves on one shared 8x8 board, and moving onto an opponent's square captures it outright while pieces also block each other's lines of movement. The entire game state is shared — there is no private player board or resource.

scoring.how_you_win: There is no point score; you win by checkmating the opponent's king (or they resign or run out of time), with no tally involved.
